name: Unruly
rules: Fill every cell with one of two colours. Never three of the same colour in a row or column, and every row and column ends up half of each.
technique.1: These two neighbours are already the same colour, so the cell just past them must be the other one: three the same in a row is never allowed.
technique.2: These two cells are the same colour with one gap between them, so the cell in the gap must be the other one: three the same in a row is never allowed.
technique.3: This line has all the cells it is allowed of one colour and is one short of the other, so its last empty cell must be that other colour.
technique.4: This line already has as many of this colour as it is allowed, so every cell still empty in it must be the other colour.
technique.5: This line needs exactly one more of one colour, and putting it outside these three cells would leave three of the other colour in a row here, so every empty cell elsewhere in the line takes the other colour.
demo.1: Fill every cell orange or purple. The ringed ones are given, so those you cannot change.
demo.2: Never three of the same colour in a row, across or down. That is one orange too many.
demo.3: Every row and column ends up three of each colour. This row has four purples.
demo.4: Two oranges with a gap. Orange in between would make three, so it has to be purple.
demo.5: Every cell filled, no run of three, and three of each colour in every row and column.
hint.pairEnd.row: The outlined cells in row {line} are side by side and both {colour}. Making the ? cell {colour} too would put three {colour} in a line, so it must be {other}.
hint.pairEnd.column: The outlined cells in column {line} are one above the other and both {colour}. Making the ? cell {colour} too would put three {colour} in a line, so it must be {other}.
hint.pairGap.row: The outlined cells in row {line} are both {colour}, with the ? cell between them. Making it {colour} too would put three {colour} in a line, so it must be {other}.
hint.pairGap.column: The outlined cells in column {line} are both {colour}, with the ? cell between them. Making it {colour} too would put three {colour} in a line, so it must be {other}.
hint.lastGap.row: Row {line} already has all {count} of its {colour} cells and is one {other} short, so its last empty cell must be {other}.
hint.lastGap.column: Column {line} already has all {count} of its {colour} cells and is one {other} short, so its last empty cell must be {other}.
hint.lineFull.row: Row {line} already has all {count} of its {colour} cells, outlined, so every ? cell in it must be {other}.
hint.lineFull.column: Column {line} already has all {count} of its {colour} cells, outlined, so every ? cell in it must be {other}.
hint.lastInRun.row: Row {line} needs just one more {colour}, and it must go in the outlined cells in columns {from} to {to}: anywhere else would leave those three all {other}. So every ? cell must be {other}.
hint.lastInRun.column: Column {line} needs just one more {colour}, and it must go in the outlined cells in rows {from} to {to}: anywhere else would leave those three all {other}. So every ? cell must be {other}.
